# Problem Statement

The committed pre-push hook at `.githooks/pre-push` has evolved to v4, but a stale v2 copy lingers at `.git/hooks/pre-push` (an untracked, orphaned artifact from a prior hooksPath configuration). The `core.hooksPath` is already correctly set to `.githooks`, so the active hook is the committed v4. The only remaining work is to remove the orphaned v2 file to eliminate confusion.

## Users

- Developer agents running `git push` in this repo — they benefit from a clean, unambiguous hooks configuration.
- Operator reviewing hook state — a clean state prevents misdiagnosis of drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `.git/hooks/pre-push` (the orphaned v2) is removed, and `git config core.hooksPath` returns `.githooks`.
- AC2: The active pre-push hook is the committed `.githooks/pre-push` v4 (verified by `git config core.hooksPath` and inspecting the active hook).
- AC3: No regression to worklog sync, branch policy, context-budget gate, or full-suite gate in the active hook.

## Impact

Developer agents see a clean hooks configuration with no stale or conflicting hook files.

## Constraints

- Must not remove the committed `.githooks/pre-push` v4.
- Must not change `core.hooksPath` (already correct).
- Must not modify or re-install `.git/hooks/` files (the directory is now a no-op since `core.hooksPath` redirects).

## Existing State

- `core.hooksPath = .githooks` (correct, set by prior work on SA-0MSN2LIOQ004TON1).
- `.githooks/pre-push` is v4 (committed, mode 755, contains worklog sync + branch policy + context-budget gate + full-suite gate).
- `.git/hooks/pre-push` is an orphaned v2 file (1,038 B, dated 2026-08-12, untracked, not active).

## Desired Change

Remove `.git/hooks/pre-push` to eliminate the stale v2 artifact.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.git/hooks/pre-push` — Remove this file (orphaned v2).
- `.githooks/pre-push` — Confirm v4 is intact (read-only check).
- `.git/config` — Confirm `core.hooksPath = .githooks` (read-only check).

## Related Work

- SA-0MSN2LIOQ004TON1 — Activate the context-budget pre-push gate in active git hooks (completed, set `core.hooksPath`).
- Discovered-from: SA-0MSN2LIOQ004TON1 (identified during audit).

## Goal

As an agent running the changed-scope test gate, I want a changed `tests/unit/test-*.mjs` file to select the node suite for that directory, so a JS/TS test edit is actually executed before commit instead of only at the push-time full suite.

## Problem

`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_is_test_file()` recognises `test_*.py`, `*_test.py`, `*.test.mjs` and `*_test.mjs` but **not** the repo's dominant node convention `test-*.mjs`. Consequences:

1. A changed `tests/unit/test-*.mjs` file is not classified as a test file, so `map_changed_to_tests()` tries the convention mapping instead (`test_<stem>.py` etc.) and selects nothing.
2. The same filter builds the `all_tests` pool used by import-graph expansion, so `test-*.mjs` files can never be selected there either.
3. Emission of a node command requires a selected `.mjs` path, so no `node --test` command is produced at all.

Verified while delivering SA-0MVTU1WHS002HN1C: editing three test files (`skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_check_freshness.py`, `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`, `tests/unit/test-check-final-validation.mjs`) produced a changed-scope command containing only `pytest ...` — no `node --test`. 46 of the 47 `tests/unit/*.mjs` files use the `test-` prefix, so the gap covers almost the whole node unit suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `_is_test_file()` recognises `test-*.mjs` (and the equivalent `test-*.js`/`test-*.ts` naming) as test files.
- A unit test asserts that changing a `tests/unit/test-foo.mjs` file selects `tests/unit/test-foo.mjs` and causes a `node --test` command to be emitted by the changed-scope command builder (no pytest-only command).
- The selection never invents a path that does not exist (the existing LP-0MTZYRTNF0092JKW existence filter still applies).
- Existing changed-scope selection tests stay green; the full suite stays green.

## Constraints

- Do not widen selection to arbitrary `.mjs` helper files (e.g. `cli-helpers.mjs`); only the test-file naming conventions.
- Keep the single-source-of-truth rule: one filter function, no duplicated naming logic.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py`

## Related work

- discovered-from:SA-0MVTU1WHS002HN1C (observed while adding hermetic ship-gate tests).

data.description:
## Goal

Give every skill an explicit **tool-output budget** so an implementation session
does not burn its context window on whole-file reads and unfiltered searches
within the first ten minutes.

**User story.** As an agent running any skill (implement, audit, refactor,
plan, test, find-related, resolve-pr-comments, agent-log-review, …), I want
guidance on how much output to pull from `read`, `bash`/`rg` and `cat`, so that
I finish a task with context to spare instead of hitting compaction / losing
the earlier half of my work.

## Evidence (why this matters)

Measured on a live `implement` session in a sibling repo
(`AI_Hell`, `AH-0MWH4F375000X08G`), analysis on 2026-11-16:

| Component | Bytes | Share of context |
|---|---|---|
| System prompt (static startup) | 51 KB | 10% |
| **toolResult messages (63 calls)** | **409 KB** | **83%** |
| Assistant text + thinking (63 turns) | 34 KB | 7% |

The session reached ~712 KB (~125k tokens est.) in **8 min 34 s**. The static
startup surface was only 10% of it — the other 90% accumulated from tool output
in under nine minutes.

Eight tool calls produced 64% of all tool output (and 53% of the whole context):

| Bytes | Call | Waste |
|---|---|---|
| 50.0 KB | `cat docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json && sed -n …` | Hit the 50 KB bash cap exactly; the next call confirmed the harness never reads the field the agent was checking — the whole read was unnecessary |
| 46.7 KB | `read src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts` (whole file) | Needed one tile-label path |
| 46.2 KB | one `rg "8.2\|Hex variety\|personality\|contract\|landmark"` over the GDD with context | Mostly unrelated hits; the agent re-narrowed with `sed -n '3270,3400p'` immediately afterwards |
| 29.1 KB | `read hexRing.ts` (whole file) | Needed three field types |
| 26.3 KB | `read skill/test/SKILL.md` (whole) | ~2 KB relevant |
| 21.9 KB | `read hexRingDefinitions.test.ts` (whole) | Needed one describe block |
| 21.7 KB | `read skill/implement/SKILL.md` (whole) | Mechanically required |
| 20.5 KB | `wl show <id> --children --json` | Over-fetched, then re-fetched again after the claim |

Two secondary observations:

1. **Broad-then-narrow does not pay.** The 50 KB `cat` and 46 KB `rg` did not
   prevent ~25 further targeted greps in the same session; the exploratory
   calls added cost without removing follow-up work.
2. **The static side is already gated; the dynamic side is not.**
   `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py` +
   `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` measure the **startup** surface
   (`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`, project `AGENTS.md`, skills prose) and are enforced by
   the pre-push gate. Nothing measures or guides **runtime** tool-output
   growth, which is where 83% of this session's context went.

## Requirements

1. Add a canonical shared doc `skill/shared/tool-output-budget.md` (mirroring
   the shape of `skill/shared/background-job-etiquette.md`: single source of
   truth, short, with a "the pattern" section and worked examples). It must
   cover at minimum:
   - **Never `cat` a generated artifact** (JSON baselines, lock files, eval
     output, build logs, `worklog-data.jsonl`, threshold files). Use `jq`
     projections (`jq '.rings[0]'`, `jq 'keys'`, `jq -c '.[] | {ringIndex,
     strategy}'`), `grep -m`, `sed -n 'A,Bp'`, or `jq length` first to size the
     thing before reading it.
   - **Cap exploratory search**: `rg … -m 5` (or `-c` / `-l` first to learn the
     shape), never `-A 20` on a first pass over a large doc. Widen only after a
     count tells you the result set is small.
   - **Read code around the symbol, not the file**: `read` with
     `offset`/`limit` after a `rg -n` locates the definition; prefer `rg -n -A 15
     '<signature>'` over a whole-file read. State the expected output size
     before issuing a call whose result could exceed ~10 KB.
   - **Do not re-fetch what you already have**: `wl show` once per work item
     per session (it is already in context after the claim), and never re-read a
     skill doc already read this session.
   - **Rule of thumb**: any single tool result over ~10 KB must be justifiable;
     an unexplained 50 KB result is a defect in the call, not in the tool.
2. Roll it out to **every** tracked skill. At minimum the skills that issue
   file reads/searches as their primary loop: `implement`, `audit`, `plan`,
   `test`, `refactor`, `find-related`, `resolve-pr-comments`, `intake`,
   `agent-log-review`, `cleanup`, `code-review`, `context-audit`, `ship`,
   `triage`, `machine-hygiene`, `report`, `standup`, `test-churn`,
   `effort-and-risk`, plus `author-command`/`interview` where they read context.
   Reference the shared doc from each `skill/<name>/SKILL.md` in the
   "references"/help section (one line, not a copy).
3. Reference the shared doc from `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (the global rule list) and
   from the `docs/dev/*-skill-reference.md` files that hold the relocated
   detail for `implement`, `audit`, `plan`, `ship` and `find-related`.
4. Cross-link `docs/dev/context-budget.md`: state explicitly that the existing
   budget covers the **static** startup surface and that
   `skill/shared/tool-output-budget.md` covers the **dynamic** runtime surface,
   so future readers do not think one replaces the other.
5. Add a docs guard `tests/test_tool_output_budget_docs.py` in the style of
   `tests/test_background_job_etiquette_docs.py`: assert the shared doc exists
   and names the `jq` / `rg -m` / `read --offset` patterns; assert every
   tracked skill (via `tests/skill_inventory.py::tracked_skill_names`) that is
   in the Requirement 2 list references it; assert no skill doc still
   recommends a bare unscoped `cat <json>` over an artifact.

## Out of scope

- Changing the `read`/`bash` tool implementations or their truncation caps
  (that is the `pi` harness, not this repo).
- Extending `measure_context.py` to parse session logs for tool-output waste.
  Worth doing, but file it as a separate follow-up (see "Discovered during
  analysis" below) so this item stays a docs rollout.
- Retrofitting already-shipped AGENTS.md prose beyond the one-line reference
  plus the new global rule.

## Discovered during analysis (candidates for separate items)

- **Session-log output audit**: extend `skill/agent-log-review/` to report
  per-session tool-output waste (top-N largest `toolResult` entries, share of
  context from tool output) and auto-file improvement items — this is how the
  evidence table above was produced.
- **`wl show` payload trimming**: a `--fields`/`--brief` flag so the claim and
  review steps do not each pull ~20 KB of work-item JSON.

## Planning decisions (2026-11-17)

- **`find-related` skill-reference doc: not created.** The producer asked
  whether the skill actually needs it. It does not: `find-related/SKILL.md` is
  untrimmed (~19 KB), so no detail was ever relocated, and no
  `docs/dev/find-related-skill-reference.md` exists. AC3 was narrowed to the
  four skills that do have one.
- **`pane-triage`: no reference added.** It is not in the Requirement 2 list and
  does not use `read`/`rg`/`cat` as its primary loop (it works through `wl` and
  herdr). Skipped.
- **`context-audit`: out of scope (confirmed).** Tooling-only package
  (`scripts/` + `__init__.py`), no `SKILL.md` to reference from.
- **Context-budget gate headroom discovered during planning.** Measured
  `global_agents` = 16268 B against a 16268 B threshold, `total` = 22878 B
  against 22878 B, and `skill_implement_md` = 22,343 B against a 22,500 B cap
  (157 B headroom). The `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` rule line therefore needs a recorded
  threshold revision, not a bypass. The implement one-liner must stay under
  ~150 B or the cap also needs revising.

## Acceptance Criteria (testable)

- AC1: `skill/shared/tool-output-budget.md` exists and documents all five points — `jq` over `cat` for artefacts, `rg -m` caps with no first-pass `-A 20`, `read` with `offset`/`limit` around a located symbol, no re-fetching context already held, and the ~10 KB per-result rule of thumb.
- AC2: All 20 listed skills that ship a `SKILL.md` reference the shared tool-output budget in it.
- AC3: `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` references the shared doc from a rule line, and `docs/dev/{implement,audit,plan,ship}-skill-reference.md` each reference it where they describe reading context; no `find-related` reference doc is created.
- AC4: `docs/dev/context-budget.md` contains a static-vs-dynamic section that states the committed budget covers the static startup surface only and links `skill/shared/tool-output-budget.md`.
- AC5: `tests/test_tool_output_budget_docs.py` exists and asserts each required path individually, so deleting the shared doc or removing any single reference fails the suite.
- AC6: No `skill/*/SKILL.md` or `docs/dev/*-skill-reference.md` recommends a bare `cat <artefact>.json` over a generated artefact.
- AC7: Full suite green via the test skill; docs committed and pushed to `dev`, with the pre-push context-budget gate green and no `CONTEXT_BUDGET_SKIP=1` bypass.

## References

- Evidence session: `AI_Hell` `AH-0MWH4F375000X08G` (2026-11-16), analysis of
  `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-AI_Hell--/2026-11-16T23-20-59-866Z_*.jsonl`.
- Pattern to mirror: `skill/shared/background-job-etiquette.md` +
  `tests/test_background_job_etiquette_docs.py`, rolled out by
  SA-0MVDP5JTK009HWOT (delivered by SA-0MVCX570P003VLBK).
- Static-context side: `docs/dev/context-budget.md`,
  `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py`,
  SA-0MSJI53RX006E2PS (reduce initial LLM context).
- Related guidance: `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md`.
- Related (open): SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD (AGENTS.md STE100 instruction — session
  length and token use).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (plan session 2026-11-17)

- **Q1: `find-related` skill reference doc.** AC3 named
  `docs/dev/find-related-skill-reference.md`, but no such file exists (only
  `docs/dev/find-related-v3-analysis.md`). Should a minimal skill reference be
  created, or should the requirement be dropped?
  **Answer (producer, 2026-11-17):** "Does the skill actually need that doc?
  Probably not since things have been working without it, in which case remove
  the reference. If it is needed then create it."
  **Evidence:** `skill/find-related/SKILL.md` is 18,960 B and untrimmed, so no
  detail was relocated; there is no reference doc because one was never needed.
  **Final:** dropped from AC3; the SKILL.md one-liner (Requirement 2) is kept.

- **Q2: `pane-triage` rollout.** It lives in `skill/` but is absent from the
  Requirement 2 list. Should it receive a reference?
  **Answer (producer, 2026-11-17):** "sounds like it shouldn't — your call
  otherwise."
  **Research:** `skill/pane-triage/SKILL.md` drives the pane-close classifier via
  `wl`/herdr; it does not run `read`/`rg`/`cat` as its primary loop.
  **Final:** skipped (documented in Planning decisions).

- **Q3: `context-audit` scope.** It has `scripts/` and `__init__.py` but no
  `SKILL.md`.
  **Answer (producer, 2026-11-17):** "confirm" (out of scope).
  **Final:** excluded; AC2 is reworded to the 20 skills that ship a `SKILL.md`.
data.title: Roll out tool-output budget guidance to all skills (jq over cat, capped rg, offset/limit reads)
